# QSA scalar page-table fetch trial, 2026-10-21

Pre-coding plan. Baseline is current production source SHA256
f1c5e71a3f7d5975fa639f5081a8e16a334fc3e0bf90d508808f5ed65a716d1c,
validated by full H800 report07993da. Packed-grid is rejected; its scheduler
is not part of this experiment.

## Project truth

| Field | Frozen choice |
| --- | --- |
| Editable | Private page-table fetch candidate/kernel, current-production A/B plumbing,8 candidate gates and profile nodes, CPU proofs, docs |
| Read-only | All production code, grid/host/chunks, ten rectangular and six compact config choices, math, dtype/layout contract, TopK, native source,30 fixtures, timer/tolerances and GPU guards |
| Hypothesis | Explicitly fetch at most two unique physical page IDs per key tile instead of one ID per key column, then broadcast them across the existing column lanes |
| Scope | Rectangular score only, both BF16 and FP8; unchanged compact path. Compile-time BLOCK_N<=PAGE_SIZE enables two-page fetch; otherwise retain general per-column fetch |
| Evidence | Actual production BLOCK_N64/128 and benchmark page196 imply at most two logical pages per tile; previous empty-grid reduction did not yield stable benefit. No profiler counter establishes page-table bottleneck yet |
| Validation | CPU execute actual load/mask branch over page boundaries, table strides/bounds/invalid IDs; exact unchanged AST outside lookup;8 H800 candidate gates plus40 production iteration nodes; full profile retained |
| Benchmark | Same30 scored-prefill cases, same FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compat; kernel mode, two alternating rounds, warmup200ms/rep100ms; score/TopK/pipeline versus native plus score/pipeline versus actual current production |
| Goal | Full-pipeline per-case >=1 or near1 (proposed0.98 floor), equal-weight arithmetic mean >1.1; experimental/iteration reports do not assert formal release validation |
| Fallback | No Torch compute fallback; no new allocation, GPU preprocessing or page-table conversion in candidate. Extra reference normalization remains test-only |

## Semantic contract

| Field | Unchanged behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Inputs | Current BF16/FP8, H/D and page sizes, padded/strided Q/cache/table, nonzero query base and chunk boundaries |
| Indexing | Identical logical_page/page_offset per column; physical IDs masked by page-table bounds and num_pages, including invalid IDs |
| Math | Exact key x query FP32 dot, ReLU before real-head reduction and existing visible-column stores |
| Output | Existing int32 selected indices/-1 padding, tie/tolerance rules, caller output and None return |
| Host/TopK | Exact current public/score launcher bytecode, chunk order/workspaces and persistent_topk identity |
| Compiler specificity | Existing Triton scalar load/where and constexpr branch only; no assembly, cache policy or NVIDIA instruction |

## Paths and gates

| Path | Change | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BLOCK_N<=PAGE_SIZE | Load first_page and optional first_page+1 with scalar address masks; tl.where broadcasts the proper ID to each column | CPU equality for every live lane and no out-of-bounds unmasked table read; H800 page64/196 with BLOCK_N64 and128 |
| BLOCK_N>PAGE_SIZE | Exact original vector fetch | H800 page16 and page64/BLOCK_N128; CPU arbitrary small page sizes |
| Invalid/tail columns | Preserve all original per-column live and physical-page masks | Short visible rows, table last page, negative/too-large physical IDs and page stride2 |
| Cache/autotune | Existing aligned rectangular entry class and original ten keys/configs; compact clone uses original six | Independent caches; source pin and actual returned per-chunk config/PTX/CUBIN snapshots |
| A/B | Isolated current-production output/workspace and real public traces | Same five-stage before/after correctness and native frozen common logits; actual pipeline timings, never sums |
| Keep/revert | Production stays current until measured | Reject unstable sub-percent effects or material active regressions; static source load counts are not memory-transaction/latency measurements |

## Implementation and delivery scope

The explicit private kernel copies the exact current rectangular signature,
cache/tuner decorators, request/query/key grid and all arithmetic/masks outside
the physical-page load. The host score launcher and public API are rebound
from the original bytecode, with independent rectangular/compact caches and
the same TopK object. The new kernel is not wired into the public export.

CPU proof executes the actual new scalar/general load branch with checked fake
memory across arbitrary page sizes, both frozen block widths, partial visible
ranges, padded table strides and invalid page IDs. Replacing just that branch
with the old load recovers exact original kernel AST. The page-table variant
uses the same30 experimental full-pipeline objective and isolated current
production A/B as packed-grid; no packed scheduler or its gate is included.

H800 candidate coverage comprises6 BF16/FP8 score tests at page16/64/196,
each checking BLOCK_N64 and128 across three request/chunk splits, plus2 real
full-entry BF16/FP8 native/FP32 comparisons. Full-entry keeps padded candidate
inputs and nonzero query base, with native's logically identical page table
normalized to contiguous columns outside timing. The default iteration profile
therefore runs48 exact nodes (40 production+8 new candidates); `full` remains
available for complete production validation before integration.

Timing remains two alternating rounds with the same stage timer, thermal/PID
guards and automatic result upload. Actual compiled configs/PTX/CUBIN/static
resources for candidate and current production are captured outside timing.
There is no claim that scalar source loads reduce actual memory transactions,
register use or latency until the H800 report is inspected.

Local validation completed:208 CPU contract/orchestration tests ran (207
passed,1 skipped). Changed-file pre-commit, Python syntax, frozen-file byte
comparisons and CPU-only CLI listing of exactly48 iteration nodes passed.
There is no local Torch/Triton/CUDA installation; H800 compilation, numerical
checks, speedup and keep/revert remain pending. Delivery uses the existing
safe child-bash runner and automatically uploads reports on success/failure.

## H800 result: BF16 promising, do not integrate the unrestricted candidate

Report branch `codex/qsa-h800-results-20261021-070337`, report commit
`9dd9767c2e29937235e765f5b0971f375dbb215a`, clean tested code
`1a805f6a43e6b3795eec8507bf180eee45710db4`.
All48 iteration correctness nodes passed in183.68s (40 production+8 trial).
This is reduced iteration validation, not the full production suite and not
formal production acceptance. All30 benchmark cases completed under the same
FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility runtime. Verified75 Git blobs,
70 source snapshots against the tested commit,150 stage rows,600 latency
samples and450 guard telemetry records. Every sampled guard passed with only
permitted worker PIDs; temperatures32–51C and SM1965–1980MHz. These snapshots
do not establish continuous machine exclusivity.

| Group | Cases | Score/native | TopK/native | Pipeline/native | Score/current production | Pipeline/current production |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Upstream BF16 | 12 | 1.1122 | 0.8989 | 0.9886 | 1.0204 | 1.0094 |
| Observed BF16 | 8 | 2.6906 | 0.9066 | 1.6688 | 1.0204 | 1.0105 |
| FP8 | 10 | 1.0139 | 0.9236 | 0.9633 | 0.9973 | 1.0002 |
| All | 30 | 1.5003 | 0.9092 | 1.1616 | 1.0127 | 1.0066 |

Values are equal-weight arithmetic means of per-case ratios of two-round
latency medians. Pipeline is timed directly through the unchanged public
function bytecode, not summed from isolated score/TopK measurements. TopK
remains unchanged and is reported, not optimized.

All12 upstream BF16 cases beat current production in both rounds for both
score and pipeline. Their mean score gain is2.04%, pipeline0.94%. Observed
BF16 means are2.04% and1.05%; tail16k, tail32k and short_batch3 show positive
score/pipeline in both rounds. Conversely FP8 budget_exact score is0.9691x
(rounds0.9741/0.9641), first_chunk0.9859x (0.9833/0.9886), dominant_long0.9808x
(0.9763/0.9853), and long100k0.9575x (0.9595/0.9555). FP8 mean pipeline1.0002x
does not offset these score regressions. Long100k pipeline rounds1.0073/0.9828
are inconsistent, so do not claim a stable pipeline regression for that case.
The two compact cases use the unchanged compact path; their small timing
changes are controls, not evidence of this optimization.

Ten cases select different rectangular configurations between trial and
current production. Gains are therefore for the candidate plus its unchanged
allowed autotune set; they do not isolate instruction changes at a fixed
configuration. Some same-configuration cases also show consistent effects:
BF16 tail16k improves, FP8 budget_exact/long100k slow down. Compiled resources
for budget_exact show123->130 registers/thread, long100k226->236; shared bytes
are unchanged. Static global-load sites drop26->20 and38->32 respectively.
These are compiler resource/static-site observations, not measured traffic,
occupancy or a proven causal explanation for the latency regression.

Decision: **retain the BF16 direction for follow-up; do not integrate this
unrestricted BF16/FP8 candidate**. Current production source remains
f1c5e71a3f7d5975fa639f5081a8e16a334fc3e0bf90d508808f5ed65a716d1c.
Next suggested experiment is a dtype-gated BF16 path, leaving FP8 on the
current lookup, followed by same-current-production A/B and full validation
before integration. Do not hard-code individual benchmark case names.
A fixed-configuration comparison can distinguish tuning-selection effects.
No such follow-up code is part of this report update.

The30-case native pipeline mean1.1616 exceeds1.1, but11 cases remain below
the proposed0.98 floor (16 below1), minimum0.8641 at FP8 long100k. The full
performance goal is unmet. Avoid treating the prior packed-grid report's
native mean1.1958 as a direct before/after baseline: shortest BF16 native
pipeline stays near56us, but this run's unchanged current-production pipeline
is25.28us versus the prior candidate's15.90us; this run's new trial is25.44us.
The same-run pipeline/current-production ratio0.9937 does not support assigning
that historical shift to the page-table edit. Its cause is unproven; use the
same-worker current-production comparison for the optimization decision.

Accuracy shrank from713.06s in the preceding full trial to183.68s, about74.2%
less. First-to-last benchmark telemetry span was1395.73s (23m15.73s), so the
combined accuracy+benchmark span is26m19.41s, excluding setup/boundaries;
benchmark work itself has not become shorter.

# QSA prefill: evidence before optimization

Pre-coding board, 2026-10-22. Read Claude sessions 1b9d3d41 and14845937:
production-path attribution -> one-hypothesis probe -> representative A/A and
A/B -> full regression -> integration. Device-specific Ascend conclusions are
not H800 evidence. optimization.md/deep_opt.md are absent. This round changes
only diagnostic tools; no new optimization or production integration is claimed.

| Project truth | Frozen choice |
| --- | --- |
| Operator/reference | Existing QSA prefill API and SHA-pinned native vLLM7a877ae |
| Production | Canonical SHA256 f1c5e71a3f7d5975fa639f5081a8e16a334fc3e0bf90d508808f5ed65a716d1c |
| Candidate | Retained query-stage-joint, unchanged combined scorer and34 choices; no unroll2 |
| Editable | Profiling coordinator/capture helpers, opt-in engine hooks, focused CPU checks, wrapper and this board |
| Read-only | All kernels, tuning policies/YAML, references,30-case definitions, timers, GPU guards and tolerances |
| First active set | BF16 n1/q16384/p102400, FP8 long100k, FP8 tail112, BF16 short96 and short_batch3 |
| Timings | Independent unprofiled kernel-mode score/TopK/sequential pipeline, two rounds,200ms/100ms; canonical comparisons retained |
| Profiling | Separate worker per case, actual warmed score launchers only, native then canonical then candidate, all real chunks once; Nsight Compute optional, bounded sections and timeout |
| Autotune | Existing original keys and choices; JIT/autotune outside profiler capture; compare actual per-chunk configs and binaries against unprofiled run |
| Validation | Existing benchmark preflight, pre/post score/TopK/pipeline numerical guards, runtime/source identities; standalone pytest explicitly skipped for this unchanged-code diagnostic |
| Acceptance | Diagnostic only; five cases cannot pass full30 performance/correctness acceptance |
| Torch use | Existing benchmark inputs/references only; production untouched, no compute fallback |

| Contract | Preserved |
| --- | --- |
| Semantics | Same BF16/FP8, H/D/layout, chunk/visible/page bounds, FP32 dot and per-head ReLU/sum, output/-1/ties and unsupported behavior |
| Host/TopK | Same public entry, validation, routing, workspace and persistent_topk |
| Empty/select-all | Unchanged, excluded from this scored diagnostic subset |
| Representative routes | Existing rectangular scorer; compact remains in full30 regression, not claimed profiled here |
| Training | Existing inference-only scope |

| Path | Diagnostic | Gate/risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Independent timing | Existing engine plus identical-function A/A controls on score and pipeline for each of native/canonical/candidate | Existing timer, source, numeric and foreign-PID guards retained |
| Hardware capture | Original score functions with output stores intact; NVTX labels and cudaProfilerStart/Stop delimit only warmed score invocations | Capture is not a speedup measurement; kernel replay/cache policy differs from graph benchmark |
| Missing profiler | Record executable/version/section availability and static resources | No dynamic utilization/cache/bandwidth inference; hardware stage remains incomplete |
| Probe selection | After returned counters, identify1-3 falsifiable hypotheses | No speculative modified kernel before evidence; keep stores/dataflow observable and check boundary shapes |
| Production integration | Only after representative benefit exceeds A/A variation and full30/full correctness pass | No cumulative gain inferred from different reports |

## First H800 collection

`tools/run_qsa_prefill_profiling_h800.sh` bootstraps the existing verified
FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility profile in an isolated process. It
runs the five cases above with the original engine and adds six A/A controls
(native/canonical/candidate times score/pipeline). TopK is still reported
against the common frozen native logits. Standalone pytest is explicitly
skipped because neither implementation changes; pre/post numerical checks
and exclusive-GPU telemetry remain. This is not a production release gate.

A second process per case runs under Nsight Compute. Only the three real
score launchers execute between cudaProfilerStart/Stop; all JIT/autotuning,
validation, TopK and timing setup precede collection. Each side runs all real
chunks once, with NVTX labels. Actual chunk configs, cubin hashes, input
fingerprints and runtime identities must match the independent timing run.
The CSV must contain real metric rows and exactly three times the chunk count
in distinct kernel IDs. A mismatch/failure stops subsequent counter runs and
preserves logs. Missing ncu returns2 with `profiler_unavailable`; permission
errors or timeouts are failures, never successful hardware collection.

Sections: LaunchStats, Occupancy, SpeedOfLight, MemoryWorkloadAnalysis,
ComputeWorkloadAnalysis and SchedulerStats. Kernel replay is bounded to the
captured launches; no full section set, source sampling or TopK profiling.
`--cache-control none --clock-control none` avoids requesting cache flushes
or clock changes. These replayed kernels still do not reproduce the graph
benchmark's complete cache/scheduling context; counter duration is not a
speedup measurement. NVTX ranges identify sides; CSV kernel IDs follow their
native/canonical/candidate launch order and each side's original chunk order.
See NVIDIA's [CLI reference](https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/NsightComputeCli/index.html)
and [section descriptions](https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html).

Reports include the ordinary stage-summary/source/runtime/trace files,
`diagnostic-timings.tsv`, per-case A/A raw samples under diagnostics,
`profile-CASE.json/.txt/.csv`, and `profiling-summary.json`. The wrapper uploads
all top-level JSON/TXT/TSV/CSV files on success or failure. It does not install
profilers, modify device permissions/clocks, or kill other GPU jobs. Timeout
cleanup only kills the coordinator's own subprocess group. Initial GPU limit
remains80C. An explicit ncu executable can be provided with `--ncu /path/to/ncu`.
Use `--cases NAME ...` to narrow within these five cases without changing the
full30 benchmark table.

Next decision uses returned evidence: compare A/A and paired A/B, inspect
actual selected configs and counters, then formulate at most1-3 hypotheses.
A probe must retain observable stores, distinguish diagnostic substitutions
from equivalent implementations, and include relevant tails/chunk boundaries.
No production edit until representative improvements exceed measured noise;
then full30 and full numerical regression before integration.

## Local validation and scope

All286 `tools/test_qsa*.py` CPU checks passed using the bundled Python3.12
runtime, including nine focused profiling checks. Changed-file pre-commit,
Python compilation, shell syntax and CLI help passed. This does not establish
CUDA/Nsight compilation, permissions, counters or on-card numerical results.
The full CPU sweep exposed an existing fake-address fixture issue: eight
updated FP8 caches exceeded the old10MB spacing between synthetic independent
allocations. The production-host differential test now uses1TiB spacing; no
production alias check, workload shape or tolerance was changed.

No device-kernel source, production entry, config YAML, workload definition or
reference changed. This collection diagnoses the retained candidate; it is
not a new candidate or an optimization acceptance report.

## Returned collection ae841236: counters unavailable, timings preserved

Report `ae841236c23e7b29c76639331da7a341d83a6848`, source c362d4e,
completed all five independent timing workers. Exit2 is the explicit
`profiler_unavailable` result: `ncu=null`, `profiles=[]`. It is not a numerical
or benchmark-worker failure. Hardware counters have not been collected.

Audit verified26 report blobs,124 source snapshots against c362d4e,152 ordinary
raw timing samples,120 A/A samples and204 clean GPU observations. Temperature
33–51C and sampled SM clock1980MHz. No foreign PID rejection was observed.
The telemetry span is336.47s, not total setup/JIT duration. Full pytest was
explicitly skipped; pre/post timing numeric checks passed.

All ratios below are same-run baseline/candidate, kernel mode. The candidate
is private stage-joint, not a newly integrated production operator.

| Case | Score/native | TopK/native | Pipeline/native | Score/canonical | Pipeline/canonical |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 n1/q16384/p102400 | 1.183783 | 0.786475 | 0.981336 | 1.124731 | 1.067775 |
| BF16 short96 | 6.339250 | 0.741110 | 2.201428 | 1.007843 | 1.006870 |
| BF16 short_batch3 | 4.366801 | 1.017585 | 2.433667 | 1.046854 | 0.939458 |
| FP8 tail112 | 1.134893 | 0.963206 | 1.026438 | 1.105439 | 1.037542 |
| FP8 long100k | 1.061236 | 0.785745 | 0.909650 | 1.098643 | 1.040603 |

A/A does not remove the timing-context issue. Short96 candidate pipeline is

all perfectly centered. Keep all samples; do not silently discard these rows,
attribute differences to a compiler/cache mechanism, or treat two rounds as a
confidence interval. Independent phase medians cannot be added to bound the
pipeline speedup.

### Resume scope, frozen before implementation

| Field | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Editable | Counter-loop extraction, bounded ncu discovery, resume coordinator/wrapper and focused CPU tests/docs |
| Read-only | All original measurements, canonical/private/native kernel sources and configs, original worker, reference, timer and guards |
| Dispatch | Verify all archived original sources/tools, copy reports to a new output directory, launch original worker in profile-capture mode only |
| Runtime | Reuse original libcuda/ptxas/FlagTree/Python/GPU UUID and compiler caches; original worker still requires matching inputs/configs/binaries/runtime |
| Acceptance | Hardware diagnostic only; no benchmark rerun, new timings, production change or inferred performance acceptance |

`--resume-report /tmp/qsa-profiling-h800.Ji2cwS` preserves the returned five
measurements and A/A. It verifies the original checkout and124 source hashes,
reference and compatibility/assembler identities before copying original report
files to a fresh output folder. The new resume driver is archived separately
in resume-sources.json. Only the original c362d4e worker executes under ncu;
no old code files are overwritten. Original caches, library paths and GPU UUID
are reused so matching remains strict. If these temporary files are gone or
the original GPU is occupied, capture stops rather than rerunning benchmarks
or switching the comparison runtime.

Profiler discovery now checks PATH and bounded common /usr/local and /opt
CUDA/Nsight installation directories. `--ncu /absolute/path/to/ncu` overrides
that discovery. No package installation, sudo or device-permission change is
performed. If still absent, return2 and upload discovery status without
repeating timing. Installing/exposing Nsight Compute is then the missing
prerequisite; CUDA compatibility libraries and ptxas do not provide ncu.

Resume implementation validation:49 affected CPU checks passed (including
source/tool tamper rejection, original report/log preservation, pinned worker
paths/reference copying, missing ncu/counter failures and normal benchmark
regression checks). Changed-file pre-commit and shell syntax passed. CUDA/ncu
execution remains unverified locally; no production files/configs changed.

## Returned resume48e8a343: provision the missing profiler

Report48e8a343932f6f4db822c6b4f16647d2b6bbc849 verified30 archived blobs.
`profiling-summary.json` confirms profiler_unavailable, ncu=null, profiles=[],
independent_benchmark_rerun=false and124 verified original sources. Original

measurements or hardware-counter conclusions are available.

Before implementation, freeze the next change: only a standalone SHA-pinned
profiler provisioner, its CPU tests and the resume GPU-UUID normalization;
all original worker/kernel/timing/configuration files stay read-only. The
returned runtime UUID is bare2d17872f-4327-2beb-8049-604ecf6a3d66, whereas the
NVML/CUDA-visible guard requires GPU- prefix. Normalize either representation
to the same full UUID and reject malformed/mixed GPU records; this correction

Resume option `--prepare-ncu` searches for an existing ncu first, then downloads

The [official CUDA13.4.3 manifest](https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/redist/redistrib_13.4.3.json)

Only CLI --version/section listing is checked before the original hardware

No further benchmark/A/A/standalone pytest is run in this resume mode.

Local provisioner/UUID validation:55 affected CPU checks passed, including
size+digest validation, safe archive extraction/link rejection, local-archive
reuse without network, version metadata and bare/full GPU UUID normalization.
Changed-file pre-commit, CLI help and shell syntax passed. The real397MB Linux
archive was not downloaded/executed on the Mac; on-card loading, instrumentation
and hardware-counter permissions remain to be checked by the resumed run.

## Returned capture d9d8b953: successful first hardware capture, CSV parser bug

Reportd9d8b9535448bea349432b3392c50c0902ad61fe has34 verified blobs.
The standalone archive SHA256 matched and ncu --version/section listing passed.
The first worker (BF16 n1/q16384/p102400) and ncu both exited0. The original

Before coding, restrict this fix to long/wide CSV normalization, exact-case

GPU guard, all three side labels in the capture manifest and exactly the
expected kernel IDs. Preserve original JSON/CSV/TXT bytes and their hashes.
An invalid or partial prior capture must fail reuse, never silently pass.

Selected four-chunk configurations:
canonical TR32/BN64/KT16/W8/stages2;
candidate TR64/BN64/KT16/W4/stages1/QUERY_PARTS1.
Ranges below are per-kernel counters across the four chunks, not averages of
benchmark speedups. Shared memory is the dynamic per-CTA portion.

The independent original benchmark measured candidate/canonical score
speedup1.124731. Lower active-warp percentage does not imply lower performance:

coexist here. This is evidence of a reuse/live-state tradeoff, not a causal

Capture uses kernel replay, uncontrolled caches and unmodified clocks, so

--resume-report /tmp/qsa-profiling-h800.Ji2cwS. Reuse all12 first-case launches

## Console reporting scope (2026-10-23, before implementation)

## Complete five-case capture3621d9ca

Report3621d9cac585ca730196ffd9adc427c3b6e6d6f0 verified45 report blobs and
four resume-driver source snapshots against32bdb357. All five case captures
pass exact original case/input/config/native+canonical+candidate binary/runtime
matching and pre/post numeric checks. NVTX confirms36 total scorer launches:
12 BF16 long (reused),3 short96,3 short_batch3,6 FP8 tail112 and12 FP8 long.
There are28188 exported metric values, including device/resource attributes.
Ten boundary GPU guards were clean at30–32C; these are snapshots, not a
continuous guarantee. The independent benchmark files are byte-identical to
ae841236; no benchmark/A/A/full pytest was rerun and no new speedup is claimed.

For FP8 long100k the canonical TR64/BN64/KT16/W4/stages2 contrasts with the
candidate's same tile/warps and stages1/QUERY_PARTS2. Registers/thread226->154,
dynamic shared bytes57344->49152, active warps12.10–12.30%->17.39–18.07%,
tensor-active18.08–18.37%->19.87–20.17%, eligible warps/scheduler0.46–0.48->
0.69–0.71. These multiple changes coexist; this is not isolated causality for
query splitting. The original same-run score/native1.061236, TopK/native
0.785745 and pipeline/native0.909650 remain the performance observations.

The FP8 tail112 main chunk uses the same154-register split configuration;
its112-row tail uses the unchanged54-register small scorer. Treat those
chunks separately. Two raw L2 derived ratios on the tiny tail are101.72%
(canonical ID3) and102.94% (candidate ID5). Preserve and flag them; do not clamp
them or use them as reliable physical hit-rate evidence. Short96/short_batch3
have very low warm-cache DRAM activity, so pursue their launch/work distribution
and graph-context behavior separately rather than applying long-tile reasoning
indiscriminately. The cross-timing-segment pipeline discrepancy remains open.

Next probe priority: fix the BF16 long candidate's actual TR64/BN64/KT16/W4/
stages1 configuration and isolate query subtiles1 versus2, preserving full-D

that controlled result consider further FP8 subdivisions. Neither probe is
implemented or measured by this console-only change. No production integration
is justified by a hardware-counter improvement alone.

## Console and offline viewing

After each ordinary benchmark worker, the engine prints native/candidate
score,TopK,pipeline latencies and ratios, then canonical/candidate comparisons

The profiling wrapper saves terminal-summary.txt alongside raw reports and

# Focused QSA query-mode and BF16 pipeline controls

## Project truth (before implementation)

| Field | Frozen choice |
| --- | --- |
| Op/reference | Existing qsa_select_paged_prefill and pinned native vLLM; no single Torch API |
| Editable | New tools/qsa_prefill_query_controls.py, CPU contract tests, focused shell entry, this document; explicit optional benchmark hook/CLI/source archive |
| Read-only | Production source/exports, all kernels/YAML, frozen workloads, numeric tolerances, original timer/guard, correctness profile and TopK |
| Build/validation | Python syntax, pre-commit, CPU orchestration tests locally;46 existing iteration GPU nodes plus before/after diagnostic score/selection checks on H800 |
| Benchmark | Same FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility profile, --mode kernel; baseline/candidate us and ratios, all samples; no30-case acceptance claim |
| Active set | Only fp8_first_chunk_float8_e4m3fn and observed_short_batch3_bfloat16 |
| Aggregation | Per condition/cycle/stage ratio of medians; list all raw paired ratios, no merging with native30-case mean |
| Runtime | Two timing rounds, warmup200ms/rep100ms;4 diagnostic cycles; initial80C, case1800s, accuracy7200s, cooldown900s/10s |
| Autotune | Existing public tune unchanged; diagnostic launchers intentionally replay one existing YAML choice per issue (FP8 TR32/BN64/KT4/W4, BF16 TR8/BN64/KT4/W4; stages2/ctas1); fixed replay is an explicit exemption, not production dispatch |
| Profiler | Compiled resource identities and metadata only; no occupancy/hardware-counter claims |
| Fallback | No production change or Torch fallback; test/reference Torch permitted only in diagnostic validation |

## Semantic contract

| Field | Frozen behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Inputs | Exact two existing BF16/FP8 fixtures, layouts and page/request/chunk geometry |
| Math | Original full-D FP32 dots, ReLU before head reduction; query modes1/2 only for eligible FP8; unchanged masks and tolerances |
| Output | Existing int32 selection/-1 padding; ties follow existing reference normalization; same-buffer outputs validated per side before overwrite |
| Dtypes/promotion | BF16 or FP8 e4m3fn Q/K, FP32 scores, existing integer metadata/output |
| Scope | Diagnostic forward-only; no new unsupported/autograd/special-value promise; invalid options fail |
| Torch | Existing FP32 score/selection reference outside timing; no production import of diagnostic |

## Execution paths

| Path | Trigger | Implementation/config | Checks and risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing run | No diagnostic flag | Original benchmark and acceptance behavior | Source/CPU regression tests |
| FP8 | first_chunk | Joint JIT at fixed32/4/W4 with mode1 versus2, same chunk geometry; score only | Independent/shared/swapped buffers; validate each score before/after; no claim tuner picks correctly |
| BF16 | short_batch3 | Canonical versus joint JIT mode1 at fixed8/4/W4; score, TopK, pipeline | Each output owner validated separately before overwrite; identical TopK object |
| Schedule |4 cycles | Balanced condition positions and predecessors; rotate stage order; each pair still original2-round AB/BA timer | Record exact order and timestamps; no assumption that cache state stays constant |
| Report | Success/failure | Original upload runner, nested JSON plus per-case controls TSV | Partial results retained; diagnostic never formal production acceptance |

The four buffer conditions are A/B, B/A, A/A and B/B for baseline/candidate.
A and B are the already allocated canonical and trial chunks, including score,
TopK scratch and output. Inputs and native common TopK logits remain identical.
No extra GPU workspace, replacement timer, synthetic cache flush or cache-policy
change is introduced. Shared-buffer checks execute and validate each side on its
own, so the second launch cannot hide an invalid first result. Pipeline validation
uses the unchanged FP32 selection checker; TopK uses unchanged native common
logits checks. All validation is outside timing.

This is a controlled follow-up, not a causal proof. In particular, buffer-order
rotation and fixed geometry reduce confounders but do not equate device cache
state across launches. Interpret repeated raw samples before choosing a dispatch
policy or integrating either private optimization.

## Delivery and interpretation

Run `bash tools/run_qsa_prefill_query_controls_h800.sh --flagtree /opt/flagtree`
from a clean checkout containing this change, using the existing activated vLLM
0.31 virtualenv and QSA_STOCK_PYTHON. The runner selects an idle H800 under the

# Combined BF16 page-table and joint-query trial

## Project truth (before implementation)

| Field | Frozen choice |
| --- | --- |
| Op/reference | Existing qsa_select_paged_prefill and pinned native vLLM source; no single Torch API |
| Editable | New private combined kernel/factory, candidate GPU/CPU tests, runner, this document; candidate routing/accuracy/source archive in benchmark tools |
| Read-only | Canonical production source/exports, all existing private kernels/factories, all YAML groups,30 scored-prefill cases, original timer/guard/reference/tolerances and TopK |
| Build/validation | Local syntax/AST/math/cache/YAML/acceptance/profile tests and pre-commit; full canonical production correctness file plus combined candidate boundary/mode/all-config/full-entry checks on H800 |
| Active set | Frozen30:12 upstream BF16,8 observed BF16,10 FP8; two score-skipping cases remain excluded |
| Metric | Same-compiler --mode kernel us; native baseline/candidate; separately score,TopK,sequential pipeline; same-run current-production score/pipeline and fixed-query diagnostics retained |
| Aggregation | Equal-weight arithmetic mean of30 native pipeline ratios>1.1 and every case>=1/near1 (proposed floor0.98); experimental only, not formal production acceptance |
| Runtime |2 rounds,warmup200ms/rep100ms,initial80C; case1800s,full correctness7200s,cooldown900s/10s; automatic report upload |
| Autotune | Reuse unchanged qsa_select_paged_prefill_query_joint_score17 choices, original keys/strategy/entry/pruner; BF1610 full-query choices,FP8 all17; compact original6. No new config/YAML parameter |
| Profiler | Compiled resources/static instruction sites only; no hardware counters/occupancy proof |
| Fallback | No Torch compute fallback or new production path; no new workspace/asm/cache policy/TopK change |

## Semantic contract

| Field | Frozen behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Inputs | Existing BF16/FP8 e4m3fn,H/D,query/cache/table strides,integer metadata,nonzero query bases,chunks,invalid page/live masks |
| Math | Full-D FP32 dot per head,ReLU before real-head reduction,unchanged score scaling and tolerances; no split of reduction D |
| Outputs | Same int32 selection/-1 padding,caller output identity and None return;tied indices follow unchanged native normalization |
| Promotion/scope | Existing FP32 scores and integer outputs;forward only,unchanged exceptions/unsupported/autograd/special-value coverage |
| Host | Exact canonical score/public function bytecode;independent entries/caches;canonical public export remains canonical |
| Torch | Only existing test/benchmark references perform compute; production never imports this private trial |

## Paths

| Path | Trigger | Implementation/config | Validation and risks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 page fetch | not IS_FP8 and BLOCK_N<=PAGE_SIZE | Exact previously measured two scalar page-ID loads and broadcast, with original masks | Actual page-branch AST emulation; GPU page16/64/196,nondivisible boundaries,strided tables,all10 choices |
| General page fetch | FP8 or BLOCK_N>PAGE_SIZE | Exact original vector fetch | AST specialization recovers query-joint for FP8; GPU fallback/page-boundary tests |
| Full query | QUERY_PARTS1 or tiny/BF16 | Exact prior joint full-query path | Forced modes and all eligible configs; BF16 recovers prior page-table candidate |
| Split query | FP8,TILE_R>=32,QUERY_PARTS2 | Exact prior two-half full-D query epilogues,one K fetch | Forced modes,H/D and tail coverage,all17 FP8 choices |
| Compact/early returns | Existing dispatch | Exact canonical compact/identity paths | Full canonical suite plus combined compact/full-entry checks |
| Report | Existing query-joint diagnostics | Main5 stages,FP8 fixed mode1/2 comparison,BF16 short_batch3 swap,combined page-gate metadata | Experimental acceptance validates source/config/page metadata; full correctness before integration |

The only kernel change from query-joint is replacing the vector physical-page
load with the exact BF16-only page-table branch. Neither optimization alters the
other dtype's active math. No fixture-name dispatch is introduced. The runner
uses --accuracy-profile full: canonical production tests keep their real public
export, while new candidate tests explicitly bind the private combined module.
This validates the unchanged production contract and the modified candidate
paths; it does not replace production exports or claim production integration.

## Implementation and validation

The private score kernel reuses the existing17-choice joint YAML group. Removing
only its BF16 page-load branch recovers the exact joint score AST. Disabling the
FP8-only split path, removing the mode parameter and restoring the decorator
plumbing recovers the exact previously measured BF16 page-table score AST.
The actual page/mask AST was executed with checked fake memory for both dtypes,
page sizes1/7/16/64/96/196/256,block widths64/128,table strides1/2/3,invalid page
IDs and live/dead columns. No production or YAML file is changed.

The factory preserves canonical host bytecode and TopK identity, with separate
rectangular/compact entries and caches. Candidate selection is explicitly
`query-joint-page`. Reports retain native score/TopK/pipeline and current-production
score/pipeline comparisons, selected-tile full/split diagnostics and the one BF16
buffer swap. The combined metadata records source pin, page gate, config snapshot
and unchanged TopK; acceptance checks reuse the existing joint gates and require
this metadata too. Private results cannot claim formal production integration.

The full GPU profile runs two files: the unchanged complete canonical production
suite (through the real public export), and40 combined candidate tests. The latter
include6 forced query-mode/head-dim/full-entry nodes,8 page-boundary/full-entry
nodes,8 rectangular every-config nodes,6 compact every-config nodes and12 public
candidate-entry nodes across both dtypes,512/1/0MiB workspace budgets and both
rectangular/compact envelopes. All17 FP8 and10 BF16 rectangular choices are
explicitly checked, alongside all6 compact choices, padded strides,int64 metadata,
nonzero query bases,request/chunk tails and untouched invalid-column sentinels.
The full candidate-entry checks also compare canonical output and FP32 reference
without rebinding the real production export. These40 nodes are required to pass;
missing,duplicate,skipped or incomplete candidate families fail the full gate.

This is full canonical contract validation plus targeted full coverage of the
modified candidate paths, not a claim that every canonical parameterized test
was rerun through the private module. A separate iteration profile remains54
nodes for later work (40 canonical +14 candidate), but the delivered runner
explicitly requests full,not iteration. The30 benchmark definitions and timing
parameters remain frozen. No focused control cycles are repeated in this run.

Local validation:98 related CPU tests passed, including7 new composition/gate
checks. New kernel syntax, source pins, unchanged YAML/production/TopK identities,
profile/CLI plumbing,shell syntax,diff checks and changed-file pre-commit passed.
No local Torch/Triton/CUDA is available: H800 JIT,numerics,selected configurations
and all30 performance results remain pending. Keep the candidate private until
those results have been audited; no production integration is part of this change.

Run `bash tools/run_qsa_prefill_query_page_h800.sh --flagtree /opt/flagtree` from
a clean checkout under the existing QSA vLLM0.31 activation and QSA_STOCK_PYTHON.
The verified FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility profile is routed explicitly;
no compiler is installed into or replaced in the virtualenv. The existing runner
selects an idle H800 and uploads complete or partial JSON/TXT/TSV reports to a
result branch under a `flagtree134-query-page-*` report directory. Run the shell
entry in a child bash so test/upload failures preserve the interactive container.

## Audited H800 result: 2026-10-22 combined candidate

Report branch `codex/qsa-h800-results-20261022-015356`, report commit
`ea000eb5e1b125a301dc63abeed47ed217c386cd`, tested clean code commit
`b096e86df692da2d1c9a275c309eb5e7f9660c03`.
All75 archived files (45 unique blobs) match GitHub sizes/blob hashes. All96
source snapshots match their recorded SHA256 and tested commit; the native
source matches its pinned reference. All181 stage TSV rows agree with case JSON
and summary. All640 baseline/candidate timing samples,480 telemetry observations,
fixed-mode parameter/resource records and combined metadata were checked. The
acceptance result was recomputed. Original timing mode,AB/BA order,compiled
configuration stability,common TopK input fingerprints and same runtime identity
passed. Every observed GPU/process guard was clean; sampled temperature32–51C
and SM clock1950–1980MHz. Guards do not guarantee identical cache/timing state
between stage pairs or explain the short-batch anomaly below.

Both sides loaded the same verified FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility
profile. The actual library was
`/tmp/qsa-cuda134-compat.rl9fpx_n/root/usr/local/cuda-13.4/compat/libcuda.so.615.71.09`,
SHA256 `85a8cc8cf00419ceb295ec62c481d05b4cdbdab10f25c5375d6d24bdbe00b4d9`,
Driver API13040. The random temporary-directory suffix changes the extraction
path,not the verified library version/content. No mixed-compiler baseline was used.

### Correctness scope

261 passed,1 skipped in808.63s. Canonical production contributed221 passes and
one skip; the40 combined-candidate nodes all passed. The skipped test is
`test_noncurrent_cuda_device`,which requires a second SM90 device. That device
guard scenario remains unvalidated under the single visible GPU. Candidate
forced modes,page boundaries,all17 FP8/all10 BF16 rectangular choices,all6 compact
choices and12 budget/envelope full-entry nodes passed the exact coverage gate.
Canonical tests retain the real production public export. These results are full
canonical validation plus the40 targeted candidate nodes; they do not imply that
every canonical parameterized test was replayed through the private candidate.

Benchmark telemetry spans1465.00s (24m25s). Adding the correctness duration gives
37m53.63s,excluding setup and any gaps outside telemetry. The40-node full candidate
suite is appropriate for this combination gate; unchanged-kernel diagnostics can
use the iteration profile later. Production/YAML/exports/TopK remain unchanged.

### Performance

All ratios below are baseline median/candidate median. Groups use equal-weight
arithmetic means of individual case ratios; native sequential pipeline is timed
separately,not obtained by adding isolated stage times. Native TopK is the vLLM
CUDA baseline; candidate TopK remains repository persistent_topk.

| Cases | Count | Score/native | TopK/native | Pipeline/native | Score/current production | Pipeline/current production |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Upstream BF16 | 12 | 1.1159 | 0.8987 | 0.9895 | 1.0260 | 1.0104 |
| Observed BF16 | 8 | 2.6943 | 0.9069 | 1.6556 | 1.0233 | 0.9921 |
| FP8 | 10 | 1.0776 | 0.9238 | 0.9814 | 1.0578 | 1.0245 |
| All active | 30 | 1.5241 | 0.9093 | 1.1644 | 1.0358 | 1.0102 |

Native pipeline mean1.1644 exceeds1.1,but16/30 cases remain below1 and10 below
the proposed0.98 floor. Minimum0.8901 is FP8 long100k. The compound objective is
not met. The private result is measurement-valid under the existing report
checks,but is not formal production acceptance. Do not delete the anomalous
short_batch3 result or substitute its swapped-buffer replay in these aggregates.

Same-run current-production comparisons retain the useful gain evidence:
BF16's20 cases average score1.0249/pipeline1.0030; FP8's10 average
score1.0578/pipeline1.0245. Across30,score1.0358/pipeline1.0102. Twenty-three
cases improve in both paired rounds for score/current-production,and23 for
pipeline/current-production. These are combined kernel plus independently tuned
configuration results,not an isolation of the page-load instruction change alone.
Thirteen cases select different non-mode tile geometry from current production.
FP8 first_chunk and short_tail select mode2 again; first_chunk's fixed comparison
is1.0029 with rounds1.0132/0.9926,and short_tail0.9879 with0.9768/0.9991.
Small-mode selection remains sensitive; no fixture-specific dispatch is justified.

The prior joint-only native pipeline mean1.1878 versus this1.1644 must not be
interpreted as an incremental combination regression. For example,short96's
native pipeline is56.992us versus candidate16.240us in that prior run; here it is
56.416us versus26.816us. Its same-run current production is26.336us versus
candidate26.496us (0.9940),so the large cross-run absolute shift is also present
in the unchanged production path. This demonstrates cross-run state sensitivity,
not its cause. Always keep the within-run comparisons and raw timings visible.

### BF16 short_batch3 anomaly recurred

At fixed TR8/BN64/KT4/W4,canonical and combined share the same tile geometry
(the candidate adds QUERY_PARTS1) and TopK object. Score/current-production is
1.0420 in both paired rounds (1.0445/1.0396),but the normal pipeline comparison
is0.8843 and the swapped replay1.0136. Actual samples are:

| Comparison | Baseline us round1/2 | Candidate us round1/2 | Ratio of medians | Paired ratios |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Native pipeline | 62.144/62.080 | 22.240/22.368 | 2.7848 | 2.7942/2.7754 |
| Current production,normal buffers | 27.328/22.816 | 28.992/27.712 | 0.8843 | 0.9426/0.8233 |
| Current production,swapped buffers | 22.720/22.752 | 22.432/22.432 | 1.0136 | 1.0128/1.0143 |

The normal paired ratios span14.49% (max/min minus1). Candidate latency shifts
from22.304us in the native comparison to28.352us in the normal production
comparison,and22.432us on the swapped replay; these use the same candidate source.
This requires investigation before production integration. Last round's focused
controls exercised joint-only code,not this combined candidate,and cannot clear
its regression. Earlier joint-only controls failing to reproduce the large loss
also do not prove it was noise or identify its cause now.

Canonical/candidate score resources at this tile are66/58 registers,0/0 spills
and43008/43008 shared bytes. Static PTX global-load sites drop27 to13; this is a
static site count,not a measured memory transaction/bandwidth or occupancy claim.
Buffer shape/stride/alignment metadata agree,but addresses/order/cache effects
are not separately established. The normal and swapped stages execute at
different times. No compiler,cache,address or TopK root cause has been proven.

iteration deliberately leaves TopK unchanged. Stage ratios cannot be added to
predict pipeline ratios or used to establish a score-only optimization ceiling.

### Decision and next step

Retain the combined private candidate as a promising direction,but do not
integrate it into the canonical production operator yet. Full correctness passed
within the declared scope; the per-case performance objective and the recurring
short_batch3 comparison still need work.

The next useful diagnostic is a focused run on the combined candidate,extending
the existing balanced buffer/order controls with canonical/canonical and
candidate/candidate self-comparisons on identical buffers. This distinguishes
repeatability of code differences from the measurement context without changing
the existing kernel timer or suppressing original data. Include short96 if
investigating the cross-run absolute pipeline shifts. Reuse the unchanged kernel
and iteration correctness gate instead of rerunning the full suite and30 cases
for this diagnostic. Keep two paired rounds and record all cycles,TopK and
pipeline samples. Do not change TopK or add case-name dispatch while the cause
remains uncertain. Further production integration requires audited representative

# QSA query subtiles trial, 2026-10-21

Pre-coding plan. Current production remains pinned to SHA256
f1c5e71a3f7d5975fa639f5081a8e16a334fc3e0bf90d508808f5ed65a716d1c.
The BF16 page-table candidate remains separate pending full validation. This
experiment isolates query subtiles against actual current production, without
stacking that candidate. workflow.md applies; optimization.md/deep_opt.md are
absent. No GPU profiler measurements are available locally.

## Project truth

| Field | Frozen choice |
| --- | --- |
| Operator/reference | qsa_select_paged_prefill; existing pinned native vLLM, no single torch API |
| Editable | Private query-split kernel/factory, fixed-config comparison helper, benchmark selection/diagnostics, CPU/GPU gates and docs |
| Read-only | Production/exports/YAML, all previous kernels, TopK,30 scored-prefill fixtures, native/reference tolerances and timers/guards |
| Evidence/hypothesis | FP8 TILE_R64/K_TILES16 compiled at226 registers/thread; split FP32 dot results into two query halves with immediate per-half head reduction/store, aiming to reduce simultaneously live accumulators. Register pressure is not a proven bottleneck |
| Autotune | Existing ten rectangular/six compact choices, original keys/strategy/aligned entry class; no new performance parameter. Fixed-config stage inherits each actual baseline chunk's configuration, then independent original autotuning remains for main comparisons |
| Active set/metric | Same30, FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility runtime, kernel mode/us/baseline divided by candidate, pipeline primary: equal-weight mean>1.1, per-case>=1 or near1 (proposed0.98 floor); score/TopK always reported |
| Validation/build | Local AST and executable CPU contracts, Python syntax and pre-commit; GPU JIT/numerical checks on H800.40 production iteration nodes plus candidate score/full-entry nodes; full profile before integration |
| Timing | Two alternating rounds, warmup200ms/rep100ms, initial80C, case1800s/accuracy7200s/cooldown900s interval10s; current five stages plus fixed-config score comparison for FP8 rectangular calls eligible to split |
| Profiler | Same collected register/spill/shared/static PTX diagnostics; no hardware-counter/occupancy/traffic claim |
| Fallback/integration | No Torch compute fallback or GPU preprocessing/extra workspace; private experiment, no production export change |

## Semantic contract

| Field | Unchanged behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Inputs | Existing BF16/FP8 e4m3fn, parameterized H/D, query/cache/table strides, pages, nonzero query base/chunk offsets and tail rows |
| Math | Each output retains one full-D FP32 dot, ReLU per real head before head sum; no splitting/reordering D accumulation or changing tolerances |
| Output | Existing int32 indices/-1 padding, caller output and None return; invalid-page/live/store masks and unspecified tie ordering |
| Special/unsupported | Existing validation/NaN/Inf/tie treatment, forward-only/no autograd promises, no new dtype or layout scope |
| Host | Original launcher/public bytecode, grids/chunks/workspaces and persistent_topk identity |
| Torch | Test/reference only; none in candidate compute |

## Paths and gates

| Path | Condition | Implementation/config | Coverage/risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Split | IS_FP8 and TILE_R>=32 | Two half-query loads outside key loop, keys loaded once per key tile; two sequential full-D dot/ReLU/head-sum/store epilogues; same whole TILE_R grid and ten configs | Direct fixed configs TILE_R32/64, uneven request/chunk tails, padded H/D and stride2; compiler can reschedule, so register savings not guaranteed |
| Original | BF16 or TILE_R<32 | Exact original query load/dot/epilogue, original vector page lookup | BF16 controls and FP8 TILE_R8; original path AST proof |
| Compact/early return | Existing gate | Exact existing kernel/API | Existing production checks; no benefit attributed |
| Fixed-config score | FP8 rectangular baseline has eligible tile | Rebind identical original host bytecode with per-chunk fixed entry launchers, baseline original JIT and candidate split JIT, exact same configs, separate existing workspaces | Untimed resource capture and before/after existing FP32 score checks; compare to independently tuned main stages, never conflate |
| Keep/revert | Full validated same-runtime data | Preserve only stable measured gains without material regressions; full correctness before integration | Two live query operands, extra instructions/layout moves or compiler scheduling may erase gains |

## Implementation and local validation

The split path loads two contiguous half-query operands outside the key loop.
The existing visible vector is reshaped/transposed/split into matching halves,
without extra global visibility reads. Each key tile is fetched once and used
by both full-D dots. Each half immediately applies the original ReLU/head-sum
and visible/invalid-page stores. Source ordering is not a guarantee that the
compiler will keep accumulator lifetimes short; resource/latency data decide.
The original BF16/tiny-tile branches are AST-identical after constexpr path
selection. The compact kernel, original host/public bytecode, config set/keys,
TopK, workspaces, chunking, shape set and numeric tolerances are unchanged.
No Torch compute/copy/cast fallback was introduced (the kernel `.to(tl.int64)`
is the existing Triton address cast).

The supplemental `score_matched` stage uses a separate pair of modules with
the exact original host bytecode and per-chunk fixed launchers. Both sides
inherit actual baseline public-entry configurations and their existing
independent workspace buffers. The baseline uses original JIT and candidate
uses split JIT. Unknown chunks, omitted preparation, config mismatches or new
compilation keys after freezing fail the trial. Fixed kernels are warmed and
resource-snapshotted outside timing, FP32-checked before/after timing, and the
fixed comparison is measured first when applicable. Main five independently
autotuned stages remain available in the same run to avoid another remote
round trip; promotion requires auditing the fixed and tuned results together.
No fixed-config score improvement is asserted before that audit.

Iteration correctness uses46 exact nodes:40 existing production+4 direct score
nodes+2 full-entry nodes. Direct score launches cover existing TILE_R8/32/64
configs, BLOCK_N64/128, K_TILES4/16, BF16 H4/D128, FP8 H4/D128,H1/D32,H3/D96,
three chunks across uneven request boundaries, nonzero query base and padded
page table/cache/query. Full-entry forces existing TILE_R64/K_TILES16/w4 so
the new FP8 path is actually executed, and reuses native/FP32 whole-output
selection gates with logically identical normalized native page table.
`--accuracy-profile full` still selects the complete production test file and
all new candidate nodes; iteration is not formal production validation.

Local result:221 CPU contract/orchestration tests ran,220 passed,1 skipped.
Proofs cover unchanged original path AST and per-half full-D dot/epilogue,
actual query address/mask execution, visibility-half mapping, host/TopK/cache
identity, fixed-config exact-key replay/freezing, report coverage and CLI
profiles. Frozen production/benchmark/previous test and kernel sources were
compared byte-for-byte, new Python syntax and diff checks passed, changed-file
pre-commit passed. No local Torch/Triton/CUDA is available. H800 JIT/numerics,
register/spill/shared/static PTX observations and performance remain pending.
The safe child-shell command uses a fresh checkout and automatically uploads
the result on success/failure. Production integration remains pending measured
benefit and complete validation.

## Completed H800 trial: useful long-FP8 gains, retain as a candidate

Report branch `codex/qsa-h800-results-20261021-085333`, report commit
`5045a0ffd10357ad47d8fae0cf7ff424ac59ccef`, clean tested code
`0ea8d13710a0895abcbfad871e26c643289132a3`. All46 exact iteration nodes
passed (40 production+6 new), including forced split full-entry FP8 and the
H1/D32,H3/D96 direct score gates. Accuracy took173.93s; this is reduced
iteration validation, not the complete production suite/formal acceptance.

Verified75 report Git blobs and80 source snapshots against tested code,
180 TSV rows (159 timed,21 fixed-stage N/A),636 raw latency samples and477
telemetry points. Runtime identity, geometry/order, source pins, independent
caches/workspaces, frozen configs, before/after numeric checks and common
native logits passed. Pinned native SHA remains
4d09eb2f409e7cd71c7849c4f3bdd71d722bce6feaccb558f7ae67ac2d489a2b.
Same verified FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4 compatibility runtime on both sides.
Every sampled guard passed with only permitted worker PIDs; temperature32–53C,
SM1965–1980MHz. Samples do not prove continuous GPU exclusivity.

Each fixed row inherits all corresponding baseline chunk configurations;
register/shared/spill records are taken from the actual direct JIT launches.
Compact/tiny tails remain unchanged. The9 applicable fixed comparisons average

Decision: **retain the query-subtile direction as a private candidate, do not
integrate the unconditional FP8 TILE_R>=32 policy**. Next suggested step is

choices, preserving a full-query option for regressing regions rather than

## Semantic contract

first half; stage1 choices form the second. All non-stage parameters are paired

page/H/D/dtype and stride keys,not workload names or a new backend threshold.

# QSA prefill tuning round 1

Pre-coding plan, 2026-10-21. Hypothesis: the current rectangular tuning set
omits the native FP8 TR32/BN64/KT16/warps8 choice. Add that choice and a
TR32/BN64/KT4/warps8 control, preserving the previous eight choices.
The three-round H800 run has completed in report4f7bfe3:219 passed, one skip,
all30 cases measured. Overall pipeline arithmetic mean1.19464x exceeds1.1,
but11 cases are below0.98, so the full goal is not met. See
[the audited results and round-count analysis](qsa_prefill_round1_h800_results.md).
Subsequent routine runs default to two alternating rounds; boundary cases need
additional confirmation. The tables below preserve the original three-round plan.

## Project truth

| Field | Frozen choice |
| --- | --- |
| API/reference | Existing qsa_select_paged_prefill; pinned native vLLM 7a877ae34dcf4a7d46de08eb16db4699e1e0047c, existing SHA256; no equivalent single Torch op |
| Editable | New NVIDIA rectangular tuning group and production decorator selection, tuning pin, every-config tests, old-eight test/benchmark clone, scored30 suite, stage runner/report plumbing and docs |
| Read-only | Device arithmetic, host dispatch and chunking, compact six configs, previous rectangular eight configs, TopK, native source, all32 fixture definitions/geometry, numerical tolerances and timer |
| Build | Local Python/shell syntax and pre-commit; H800 JIT/autotuning outside reported stage timings |
| Validation | Existing official native/FP32/unsupported/alias/device coverage; every rectangular config across BF16/FP8/H/D/layout/chunk boundaries; actual public entry, previous-eight equivalence and CPU report contracts |
| Benchmark | Same verified FlagTree/ptxas13.4/CUDA13.4compat; --candidate production --suite scored-prefill --mode kernel; native score/TopK/pipeline plus old-eight score/pipeline paired in the same worker |
| Active set | 30 scored cases: upstream12 BF16 + observed8 BF16 + FP8 ten; select-all single and batch18 remain functional/diagnostic fixtures but leave the standard benchmark and acceptance set |
| Metric | Primary: native complete sequential GPU pipeline / production pipeline, including TopK; score and common-logits TopK remain separately reported; Python validation/allocation excluded as before |
| Aggregation | Equal-weight arithmetic mean over exactly30 native/production pipeline ratios >1.1; per-case >=1 or near1; report >=0.98 as the proposed near1 threshold explicitly, not a statistical significance test; retain subgroup geometric means for diagnosis |
| Timeout/timing | Three alternating rounds, warmup200ms/rep100ms, worker1800s, full accuracy7200s, initial80C, cooldown900s/10s; unchanged foreign-PID/thermal guards |
| Profiler | Existing ncu/nsys discovery, compiled resources/PTX/CUBIN and actual config snapshots; tuner scans are diagnostics, not acceptance timing or hardware counters |
| Autotune | New qsa_select_paged_prefill_tuning_round1_score: original8 + native FP8 choice + KT4 control =10; existing keys including IS_FP8/default policy retained; compact group6 and historical group8 unchanged |
| Fallback | NO_TORCH_COMPUTE_FALLBACK; existing generic rectangular/compact paths and unsupported errors; no native kernel substituted into production |

## Alignment contract

| Field | Preserved contract |
| --- | --- |
| Device/input | SM90, matching BF16/FP8 E4M3FN Q/cache, parameterized H/D, existing strided metadata/page bounds/nonzero query base |
| Output | Caller-owned contiguous int32 indices and -1 padding; same None API, visible bounds and tie/numerical policy |
| Math | Same FP32 dot result, ReLU before summing real heads, FP32 logits; no casts or layout conversions introduced |
| Chunking/TopK | Same512MiB budget, chunk boundaries/order/workspaces and persistent_topk; native CUDA TopK unchanged |
| Unsupported/autograd | Existing inference-only and resource/device/dtype/layout limits unchanged |
| Reference use | Torch compute only in tests/benchmark references, never production |

## Paths and evidence

| Path | Change | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rectangular | Only decorator config-group name changes;10 choices | Exact old source recovered by reverting that literal, every-config numerical validation and new tuning-cache identity |
| Compact/empty/select-all | None | AST/body/config equality and official tests |
| Previous-eight | Test-only clone of exact current JIT/public host with frozen-eight tuner, separate LibEntry caches | Old production source SHA recovered, same TopK identity, actual old/new chunk geometry and pre/post FP32/native checks |
| Benchmark | New scored-prefill30, native three stages and previous-eight two stages | No native-reference changes, missing/failed/duplicate/select-all cases cannot produce full acceptance aggregate |
| Report | Overall arithmetic mean and per-case floor separately from technical run status | Incomplete/shared measurements cannot pass acceptance; primary complete pipeline timed independently, never summed stages |

The first card run tests the hypothesis; adding a candidate does not prove an
improvement. Retain/revert only after inspecting actual native and old-eight
pipeline ratios, each slow case, and all30 correctness/performance results.

## Implementation and local validation

The production file differs from the previous accepted file only by the
rectangular decorator's config-group literal. Replacing that literal recovers
the exact previous SHA256
6db2918b5b7dc1798244548972458a8c59745f967341a10663e2d704cf35687a.
The round1 production SHA256 is
d345e5e0eeec5de84958f0ffe81aa2ce286ce982448f6d167f94d87e02f7c849.
The compact six and historical rectangular eight config groups are unchanged.
No production Torch call, new dispatch/validation/registration, cache hint,
copy/cast, extra workspace or TopK change is introduced.

The previous-eight comparison is benchmark-only. It reuses the exact JIT and
public host bytecode, with fresh rectangular and compact LibEntry caches and
the same persistent_topk callable. Its source-equivalence pin rejects changes
beyond the config-group literal. Both sides' real public chunk sequences are
captured and checked; old-eight score and pipeline are validated against the
existing FP32/native-selection contract before and after timing. Each pipeline
has its own output/workspace, and no timings are derived by subtracting stages.

Tuner evidence records the ten/eight/six candidates and last tuning event,
outside acceptance timing. Actual compiled config/resource snapshots remain
separate. LibEntry may reuse one choice across chunks; the last tuning event
is not presented as a per-chunk exhaustive scan. Historical six/eight-choice
experiment fixtures retain their original groups and source pins.

Local validation:

```bash
PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/qsa-round1-pycache PYTHONPATH=tools \
  python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_qsa*.py'
```

186 tests ran:185 passed, one optional Torch-dependent test skipped. Config
and source pins, independent previous JIT/host binding, exact30 case selection,
20 BF16/10 FP8 dtype routing, arithmetic-vs-geometric aggregation, per-case
floor and mean gates, partial/duplicate/changed/failed/shared/nonfinite report
rejection and CLI forwarding passed. Pre-commit and syntax checks pass. Local
CPU checks do not validate GPU compilation, numerics or speedup.

## H800 run

Use the existing verified vLLM0.31 virtualenv, /opt/flagtree, ptxas13.4 and
CUDA13.4 compatibility-library wrapper. Run as a child bash, not source:

```bash
bash tools/run_qsa_prefill_flagtree_ab_h800.sh \
  --flagtree /opt/flagtree --candidate production \
  --suite scored-prefill --mode kernel --compare-previous-tuning \
  --rounds 2 --kernel-warmup-ms 200 --kernel-rep-ms 100 \
  --max-initial-temp-c 80 --timeout 1800 --accuracy-timeout 7200 \
  --cooldown-timeout 900 --cooldown-interval 10
```

Full official accuracy runs once before timing, including all ten rectangular
configs across the existing parameterized BF16/FP8 fixtures. The expected
official count remains219 passes and one second-device skip, but actual card
results are pending. The worker then separately validates and measures:

1. Native score versus formal production score.
2. Native TopK versus unchanged repository persistent_topk on common logits.
3. Native pipeline versus formal production pipeline (primary acceptance).
4. Previous-eight score versus formal production score (incremental evidence).
5. Previous-eight pipeline versus formal production pipeline (incremental evidence).

At three rounds, all30 cases produce150 stage records,900 raw samples and600
timing telemetry points. Only one full accuracy run is needed; previous-eight
diagnostics add stage timing, not a second full pytest run. Standard timing
and thermal/foreign-PID safeguards are unchanged. Shared-GPU runs remain
exploratory and cannot pass acceptance.

The existing wrapper automatically uploads JSON/TXT/TSV reports on success or
failure. It now also uploads overall-acceptance.json. Technical exit0 means
the run completed; performance success is separately reported by target_met,
requiring a complete same-run30-case set, arithmetic mean >1.1 and every
pipeline ratio >=0.98 under the explicitly proposed near-one threshold.
Subgroup geometric means remain diagnostic and do not replace this new goal.

The original run above used three rounds. Routine commands now use two rounds
based on the observed variation; one/two-round estimates in the results document
are recomputed subsets of that original report, not additional GPU runs.
The configuration remains under evaluation: the old-eight comparison contains
a0.97582x pipeline regression and the full30 goal is not yet met. No production
or tuning change is made as part of reducing the routine round count.

THREADS_PER_BLOCK = 1024

MEDIUM_HEADER_SIZE = (MEDIUN_HIST_BYTES + MEDIUM_SCALARS_BYTES + 127) & (~127)  # 3200
MAX_BUFFERED_ITEMS = 4096

FIXED_SMEM_LARGE = ((RADIX + RADIX + 5) * 4 + 15) & (~15)  # 2080
# Medium path with bin replay needs up to 32768 uint32 of shared_ordered.
# SMEM_MEDIUM_QUAD_C = 32768 → 128KB. Must fit within max_smem_per_block.
MEDIUM_REPLAY_SMEM = 32768 * 4  # 131072 bytes
# Medium/decode paths reuse shared_ordered's smem (mirroring vLLM's single
# extern __shared__ buffer). SMEM_MEDIUM // 4 = 8992 uint32s cover both the
# medium layout (8992) and the decode layout (8192).
SMEM_MEDIUM_QUAD = SMEM_MEDIUM // 4  # 8992
# Decode path layout constants (see histogram_2048_topk in persistent_topk.cuh)
DECODE_SBASE = 8192 - 8  # 8184
DECODE_RHIST = RADIX + 128  # 384
DECODE_BOFF = 2 * DECODE_RHIST  # 768
DECODE_DBUF = (DECODE_SBASE - DECODE_BOFF) // 2  # 3708

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@triton.jit
def _convert_to_uint32_v2(x):
    bits = x.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True)
    return tl.where((bits & 0x80000000) != 0, ~bits, (bits | 0x80000000))


@triton.jit
def _convert_to_uint8(x):
    # FP16 high 8 bits -> 256-bin coarse key (order-preserving).
    h = x.to(tl.float16)
    bits = h.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)
    key = tl.where((bits & 0x8000) != 0, ~bits, bits | 0x8000)
    return (key >> 8).to(tl.int32)


@triton.jit
def _decode_bin(x):
    # FP16 high 11 bits -> 2048-bin decode key (order-preserving).
    h = x.to(tl.float16)
    bits = h.to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)
    key = tl.where((bits & 0x8000) != 0, ~bits, bits | 0x8000)
    return (key >> 5).to(tl.int32)


@triton.jit
def _barrier_with_atomic_add(
    arrival_counter_ptr,
    zeros,
    lane,
    thresold,
):
    tl.atomic_add(
        arrival_counter_ptr + zeros,
        1,
        mask=lane == 0,
        sem="release",
        scope="gpu",
    )
    # TODO: every thread query, no following debug_barrier needed
    arrival_counter = tl.atomic_add(
        arrival_counter_ptr,
        0,
        sem="acquire",
        scope="gpu",
    )
    while arrival_counter < thresold:
        arrival_counter = tl.atomic_add(
            arrival_counter_ptr,
            0,
            sem="acquire",
            scope="gpu",
        )


# Extracted from persistent_topk.cuh in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm
@triton.jit
def _radix_topk(
    row_input,
    row_output,
    seq_len,
    my_chunk_start,
    CHUNK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    local_histogram_ptr,
    suffix_sum_ptr,
    shared_scalars_ptr,
    shared_ordered_ptr,
    g_histogram_ptr,
    g_state_ptr,
    cta_in_group,
    ctas_per_group,
    barrier_phase,
    iter_idx,
    TOPK: tl.constexpr,
    VEC_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
):
    RADIX: tl.constexpr = 256

    my_chunk_end = my_chunk_start + CHUNK_SIZE
    my_chunk_end = min(my_chunk_end, seq_len)
    actual_chunk_size = my_chunk_end - my_chunk_start if my_chunk_start < seq_len else 0
    lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
    zeros = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE], dtype=tl.uint32)
    zeros_2d = tl.zeros([BLOCK_SIZE, VEC_SIZE], dtype=tl.uint32)
    vec = tl.arange(0, VEC_SIZE)

    # -- Stage 1: Load chunk to shared memory as ordered uint32 --
    # TODO: remove rem_tiles, rem_elems
    n_vec_full = actual_chunk_size // (BLOCK_SIZE * VEC_SIZE)
    rem_tiles = (actual_chunk_size - n_vec_full * BLOCK_SIZE * VEC_SIZE) // BLOCK_SIZE
    rem_elems = actual_chunk_size % BLOCK_SIZE
    for t in tl.range(0, n_vec_full):
        base = t * BLOCK_SIZE * VEC_SIZE + lane * VEC_SIZE
        offs = base[:, None] + vec[None, :]
        x = tl.load(row_input + my_chunk_start + offs)
        bits = _convert_to_uint32_v2(x)
        tl.store(shared_ordered_ptr + offs, bits)
    for t in tl.range(0, rem_tiles):
        offs = (n_vec_full * VEC_SIZE + t) * BLOCK_SIZE + lane
        x = tl.load(row_input + my_chunk_start + offs)
        bits = _convert_to_uint32_v2(x)
        tl.store(shared_ordered_ptr + offs, bits)
    if rem_elems > 0:
        offs = (n_vec_full * VEC_SIZE + rem_tiles) * BLOCK_SIZE + lane
        in_range = lane < rem_elems
        x = tl.load(
            row_input + my_chunk_start + offs, mask=in_range, other=float("-inf")
        )
        bits = _convert_to_uint32_v2(x)
        tl.store(shared_ordered_ptr + offs, bits, mask=in_range)
    tl.debug_barrier()

    # -- Init radix select state --
    tl.store(shared_scalars_ptr + zeros, 0, mask=lane == 0)  # prefix
    tl.store(shared_scalars_ptr + 1 + zeros, TOPK, mask=lane == 0)  # remaining_k
    tl.debug_barrier()

    # -- Initial barrier --
    _barrier_with_atomic_add(
        g_state_ptr + 2,
        zeros,
        lane,
        (barrier_phase + 1) * ctas_per_group,
    )
    barrier_phase += 1
    # tl.debug_barrier()

    if cta_in_group == 0:
        # Ring-slot clearing (next_hist per round) assumes every row is a radix
        # row. With non-radix rows interleaved (decode/medium/trivial), a later
        # radix row's first current_hist can read stale counts from an earlier
        # radix row. Clear all 3 slots at the start of each radix row; the
        # round-0 barrier below makes the clearing visible to all CTAs.
        tl.store(g_histogram_ptr + lane, 0, mask=lane < RADIX)
        tl.store(g_histogram_ptr + RADIX + lane, 0, mask=lane < RADIX)
        tl.store(g_histogram_ptr + 2 * RADIX + lane, 0, mask=lane < RADIX)
        tl.store(g_state_ptr + 3 + zeros, 0, mask=lane == 0)  # output_counter

    # -- Stage 2: 4 rounds of radix select --
    for round_idx in tl.static_range(0, 4):
        global_round = iter_idx * 4 + round_idx
        shift_bits = 24 - round_idx * 8
        prefix = tl.load(shared_scalars_ptr)
        remaining_k = tl.load(shared_scalars_ptr + 1)

        # current_hist inited zero in host-side or pre iter of group
        current_hist_ptr = g_histogram_ptr + (global_round % 3) * RADIX
        next_hist_ptr = g_histogram_ptr + ((global_round + 1) % 3) * RADIX

        tl.store(local_histogram_ptr + lane, 0, mask=lane < RADIX)
        tl.debug_barrier()

        # TODO: no vec load from smem
        for t in tl.range(0, n_vec_full):
            base = t * BLOCK_SIZE * VEC_SIZE + lane * VEC_SIZE
            offs = base[:, None] + vec[None, :]
            ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs)
            mask = 0 if round_idx == 0 else ((~0) << (32 - round_idx * 8))
            match = (ordered & mask) == prefix
            bucket = (ordered >> shift_bits) & 0xFF
            tl.atomic_add(
                local_histogram_ptr + bucket,
                1,
                mask=match,
                sem="relaxed",
                scope="cta",
            )
        for t in tl.range(0, rem_tiles):
            offs = (n_vec_full * VEC_SIZE + t) * BLOCK_SIZE + lane
            ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs)
            mask = 0 if round_idx == 0 else ((~0) << (32 - round_idx * 8))
            match = (ordered & mask) == prefix
            bucket = (ordered >> shift_bits) & 0xFF
            tl.atomic_add(
                local_histogram_ptr + bucket,
                1,
                mask=match,
                sem="relaxed",
                scope="cta",
            )
        if rem_elems > 0:
            offs = (n_vec_full * VEC_SIZE + rem_tiles) * BLOCK_SIZE + lane
            in_range = lane < rem_elems
            ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs, mask=in_range, other=0)
            mask = 0 if round_idx == 0 else ((~0) << (32 - round_idx * 8))
            match = (ordered & mask) == prefix
            bucket = (ordered >> shift_bits) & 0xFF
            tl.atomic_add(
                local_histogram_ptr + bucket,
                1,
                mask=match & in_range,
                sem="relaxed",
                scope="cta",
            )
        tl.debug_barrier()

        counts = tl.load(local_histogram_ptr + lane, mask=lane < RADIX)
        tl.atomic_add(
            current_hist_ptr + lane,
            counts,
            mask=(counts > 0) & (lane < RADIX),
            sem="relaxed",
            scope="gpu",
        )

        if cta_in_group == 0:
            tl.store(next_hist_ptr + lane, 0, mask=lane < RADIX)

        _barrier_with_atomic_add(
            g_state_ptr + 2,
            zeros,
            lane,
            (barrier_phase + 1) * ctas_per_group,
        )
        barrier_phase += 1
        # tl.debug_barrier()

        g_counts = tl.load(current_hist_ptr + lane, mask=lane < RADIX, other=0)
        tl.store(suffix_sum_ptr + lane, g_counts, mask=lane < RADIX)
        tl.debug_barrier()

        for t in tl.static_range(0, 8):
            val = tl.load(suffix_sum_ptr + lane, mask=lane < RADIX)
            other_offs = lane + (1 << t)
            tmp = tl.load(suffix_sum_ptr + other_offs, mask=other_offs < RADIX, other=0)
            val += tmp
            tl.debug_barrier()
            tl.store(suffix_sum_ptr + lane, val, mask=lane < RADIX)
            tl.debug_barrier()

        tl.store(shared_scalars_ptr + 2 + zeros, 0, mask=lane == 0)  # threshold_bin
        tl.store(
            shared_scalars_ptr + 3 + zeros, remaining_k, mask=lane == 0
        )  # next_remaining_k
        tl.debug_barrier()

        count_ge = tl.load(suffix_sum_ptr + lane, mask=lane < RADIX, other=0)
        count_gt = tl.load(suffix_sum_ptr + lane + 1, mask=(lane + 1) < RADIX, other=0)
        threshold_mask = (
            (count_ge >= remaining_k) & (count_gt < remaining_k) & (lane < RADIX)
        )
        tl.store(shared_scalars_ptr + 2 + zeros, lane, mask=threshold_mask)
        tl.store(
            shared_scalars_ptr + 3 + zeros, remaining_k - count_gt, mask=threshold_mask
        )
        tl.debug_barrier()

        threshold_bin = tl.load(shared_scalars_ptr + 2 + zeros, mask=lane == 0, other=0)
        new_prefix = prefix | (threshold_bin << shift_bits)
        tl.store(shared_scalars_ptr + zeros, new_prefix, mask=lane == 0)
        next_remaining_k = tl.load(
            shared_scalars_ptr + 3 + zeros, mask=lane == 0, other=0
        )
        tl.store(shared_scalars_ptr + 1 + zeros, next_remaining_k, mask=lane == 0)
        tl.debug_barrier()
    # end 4 radix rounds

    # -- Count local > pivot elements --
    ordered_pivot = tl.load(shared_scalars_ptr)
    my_gt_count = tl.full((BLOCK_SIZE,), 0, dtype=tl.uint32)
    # TODO: no vec load from smem
    for t in tl.range(0, n_vec_full):
        base = t * BLOCK_SIZE * VEC_SIZE + lane * VEC_SIZE
        offs = base[:, None] + vec[None, :]
        ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs)
        gt_mask = ordered > ordered_pivot
        my_gt_count += tl.sum(gt_mask.to(tl.uint32), axis=-1)
    for t in tl.range(0, rem_tiles):
        offs = (n_vec_full * VEC_SIZE + t) * BLOCK_SIZE + lane
        ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs)
        gt_mask = ordered > ordered_pivot
        my_gt_count += gt_mask.to(tl.uint32)
    if rem_elems > 0:
        offs = (n_vec_full * VEC_SIZE + rem_tiles) * BLOCK_SIZE + lane
        in_range = lane < rem_elems
        ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs, mask=in_range, other=0)
        gt_mask = (ordered > ordered_pivot) & in_range
        my_gt_count += gt_mask.to(tl.uint32)
    tl.debug_barrier()
    local_gt_count = tl.sum(my_gt_count)

    # -- Stage 3: Collect top-k indices --
    tl.store(local_histogram_ptr + zeros, 0, mask=lane == 0)
    gt_pos = tl.atomic_add(
        g_state_ptr + 3 + zeros,
        local_gt_count,
        mask=(lane == 0) & (local_gt_count > 0),
        sem="relaxed",
        scope="gpu",
    )
    tl.store(local_histogram_ptr + 1 + zeros, gt_pos, mask=lane == 0)
    tl.debug_barrier()
    gt_pos = tl.load(local_histogram_ptr + 1 + zeros)

    # TODO: no vec load from smem
    for t in tl.range(0, n_vec_full):
        base = t * BLOCK_SIZE * VEC_SIZE + lane * VEC_SIZE
        offs = base[:, None] + vec[None, :]
        ordered = tl.load(shared_ordered_ptr + offs)
        gt_mask = ordered > ordered_pivot
        local_pos = tl.atomic_add(
            local_histogram_ptr + zeros_2d,
            1,
            mask=gt_mask,
            sem="relaxed",
            scope="cta",
        )
        tl.store(
            row_output + gt_pos[:, None] + local_pos,
            my_chunk_start + offs,
            mask=gt_mask,
        )
    for t in tl.range(0, rem_tiles):
